collected_dynamic_variables.pain_frame: Missed calls when I close early
collected_dynamic_variables.interest_topic: How does this whole thing work exactly?; I sometimes miss calls when I close early, so I'm curious about what you offer.
collected_dynamic_variables.pain_points: Missed calls when closing early, Callers don’t leave voicemail and go to competitors/next store, Callers are checking stock availability, Callers sometimes want to place an order, Wants to capture request + contact info for follow-up
collected_dynamic_variables.call_volume: a few each week when I close early

transcript:
User: Hi, I got a flyer. How does this whole thing work exactly?
Agent: Got it — you saw the flyer and you’re wondering how it works. What made you start looking into this right now?
User: I sometimes miss calls when I close early, so I'm curious about what you offer.
Agent: Makes sense — if you close early, those calls can just ring out. When that happens, do people usually leave a voicemail, or do they just call the next place?
User: Most don't leave a voicemail; they probably just move on to the next store.
Agent: Yeah, I hear you—if they don’t leave a message, it’s basically gone. Roughly how many calls a week do you think you miss when you close early?
User: It's hard to say exactly, but maybe a few each week when I close early.
Agent: Got it — a few a week adds up fast if they’re just moving on. What kind of business is this for?
User: It's a hardware store I own. Just exploring options to see if this could help.
Agent: Got it — hardware store, that makes sense. When you do miss a call, is it usually someone checking if you have a specific item in stock, or more like placing an order for pickup/delivery?
User: Mostly checking if we have a specific item in stock. Sometimes they want to place an order, though.
Agent: Makes total sense — those “do you have it?” calls are usually a quick yes/no, and if they can’t reach you they just buy somewhere else. Mind if I do a quick 30‑second calculation on what those missed calls could be costing you?
User: I get that, but I'm still just gathering information right now. Not ready for calculations yet.
Agent: Totally fair — we can skip the math. When you close early and miss a call, what would you want to happen instead: capture their item request and contact info so you can call them back, or let them place an order right then?
User: Probably capturing their request and contact info would be helpful, so I can follow up later.
Agent: Got it — so even if you’re closed, you’d want to grab what they need and how to reach them so you can win it back. When you’re not able to answer, do you want it to send you that request instantly so you can call them back, or just keep a list for the next morning?
User: A list for the next morning would be fine. I'm just thinking about possibilities right now.
Agent: Makes sense — keep it simple and just have a clean list waiting in the morning. When someone calls after hours, do you want it to also tell them your hours and location while it grabs their item request and number?
User: Yeah, that could be useful. But how does this integrate with my existing phone line?
Agent: Yeah, totally — we usually connect by forwarding your existing line (or just after-hours) to Dialux, so callers hit the same number and you keep your current carrier. Is your phone setup a landline, a VoIP system, or a cell line you use for the store?
User: It's a landline. So, this wouldn't require changing my current phone carrier or setup, right?
Agent: Got it — landline. Right, in most cases you don’t need to change carriers; we can set it up with call forwarding so your existing number and setup stay the same. Do you already have after-hours or “close early” forwarding set up with your phone company today?
User: No, I don't have any forwarding set up right now. Just looking into options at the moment.
Agent: Got it — so right now it just rings out when you’re closed early. If you could add one simple after-hours message plus a way for them to leave their item request and callback number, would you want that to run only when you close early, or every day after normal closing time too?
User: Possibly just when I close early. Still weighing if this would suit my needs though.
Agent: Got it — only on those early-close days. What would make you feel confident this fits: capturing more callbacks, stopping people from going to the next store, or just not having to think about the phones at all?
User: Mostly capturing callbacks and stopping them from moving on. But I need to think it over more.
Agent: Makes sense — if you can capture the callback, you’ve got a real shot at saving the sale. What’s the one thing you’d need to know to decide whether this is worth exploring further?
User: I'd need to know if there are any long-term contracts or hidden fees involved.
Agent: Got it — you’re basically trying to avoid getting locked into something or surprised later. When you say “contract,” are you most worried about being stuck for a year, or more about extra charges that pop up after you start?
User: I'm concerned about both long-term commitment and unexpected charges. Just want to be sure before deciding.
Agent: Makes sense — nobody wants surprises or to feel locked in. If we keep it high-level here and Jay walks you through the exact terms and what’s included so it’s all clear upfront, would that be worth exploring?
User: I appreciate that, but I really need to think about it first. I'll call back if I decide.
Agent: Fair — what specifically do you need to think about: the commitment/fees side, or whether it’ll actually capture enough callbacks to be worth it?
User: More about if it captures enough callbacks for it to be worth it. I'll mull it over.
Agent: Got it — it really comes down to whether it’ll actually save those “do you have it?” calls instead of losing them to the next store. Before you go, when someone calls after hours, do you want the message to ask what item they need plus their name and number, or also their preferred pickup time?
User: Just their name, number, and the item they need. I'll consider it, though. Thanks for the info.
Agent: Got it — name, number, and the item they need keeps it simple. Thanks for calling, and if you decide you want to explore it further, we can walk through what that would look like for your landline setup—take care.
